meta.purpose: Party identity is not stable across years. This file records the moments when a name stopped meaning the same organisation, so a chart cannot silently compare two different things.
meta.rule: A series that keeps two merged parties separate, or that treats a renamed party as a new one, tells a lie the source never told. The register files 2020-2024 as two separate legal parties because that is what they were; it does not know about 2026.

groups.name: PRO (Progressief Nederland)
groups.note: GroenLinks and PvdA filed separate Wfpp reports every year in this dataset. From 2023 they campaigned on one list and sat as one parliamentary group, and from 1 July 2026 they are one legal party. Reading their rows as two independent parties is correct for 2020-2022, arguable for 2023-2025, and wrong from 2026.

events.what: Members of both parties vote for a joint electoral list: 91.8% of GroenLinks, over 87% of PvdA.
The two Tweede Kamer groups merge into one group, GroenLinks-PvdA.

First joint election: one list, 25 seats, Frans Timmermans leader. Under Wfpp art. 10 a combined list shares the base amounts pro rata, so the 2023 subsidy rows describe one list, not two independent parties.
Online referendum approves a full merger: 88% of PvdA members, 89% of GroenLinks members.
The new name is announced: Progressief Nederland, abbreviated PRO.
The Tweede Kamer group changes its name to Progressief Nederland.
Founding congress adopts the principles programme, statutes and rules of procedure.
Progressief Nederland is founded. GroenLinks and PvdA cease to exist as separate parties.
